items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: At that time he was four years old, that was on the centerfold of the New York Times along with Crown Prince Hirohito, who was 16 years old.

ctx.x: You and I are only a few years apart, and I have some vivid memories of what grabbed me as a kid musically, and I’m wondering what grabbed you?

Well first of all my father, who was that man there, was a musician. And I was born on March 14, 1945 in Sydney, New York, and we lived in Unadilla, New York. And he quit playing. At that time he was four years old, that was on the centerfold of the New York Times along with Crown Prince Hirohito, who was 16 years old. I’ve got the original newspaper upstairs. It’s just barely holding together. But he quit playing drums when he was about five. I mean you can see by those drums, I mean with that gooseneck hanging…

there, I’ll tell you about the other one which I got later on. But I was always rocking. I just always loved to rock. Even in a car, even in a straight chair I rock. I don’t know why but I do. But the music was always in the house. And my uncle was a bass player, my grandfather — who lived to be 100 — was a violin player and a shoemaker, and his wife, my grandmother, my father’s mother, was a pianist — not a jazz pianist but a pianist, and they played the theater circuit with this fascination of a 4-year-old…
